description: Agent-facing journal tiers for the local sociology and demography literature database. The full archive remains in articles.json; this file controls default screening and escalation.

abstract_policy.default_screening: Use title plus abstract_preview first. Load full abstracts only for narrowed candidates.

core_default.purpose: Main sociology, demography, family, gender, stratification, education, and China-facing journal pool.
journals: British Journal of Sociology of Education
Research in Social Stratification and Mobility

review_anchor.purpose: Review and map-making sources. Use for conceptual orientation, not as evidence that a specific empirical claim is settled.

adjacent_recent.purpose: Adjacent or broad journals included in default screening only for recent records unless a targeted reason exists.

rules.reason: Life-course mechanism anchor; current local records often lack abstracts, so use mainly as title-level routing.
Broad sociology journal; recent records are useful for positioning, older records should be targeted.
Useful for norms, identity, fairness, and interactional mechanisms.
Broad quantitative social science; use recent records by default.
Very large and broad quality-of-life/social indicators journal. Recent records are included for construct and background searches; older records are archive-only.
Important demographic journal, but broad and currently mostly title-only in this archive. Recent records are included; older records are archive-only.
Broad sociology journal; use recent records by default.
Review-style journal with long abstracts. Use recent records by default; older review records are targeted only.
Work, occupation, and labor-market mechanisms; use when employment or job structure is relevant.
Labor and work-family adjacency; recent records only by default.

archive_on_demand.purpose: Large, broad, old, or lower-priority material. Search only for targeted gaps, reviewer-risk checks, or explicit user requests.

open_search_triggers: A likely reviewer literature family is missing from the local pool.
The local pool has no direct core conversation for the empirical finding.
The project requires non-sociology fields such as economics, psychology, public health, policy, or area studies.
A user explicitly asks for a broader or systematic search.
